newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Yieh Phui plans US$90 mln convertibles.
newsitem.headline: Yieh Phui plans US$90 mln convertibles.

text.p: Yieh Phui Enterprise, one of Taiwan's leading steel makers, said on Monday it plans to issue US$90 million worth of convertible bonds in June in Luxembourg to raise funds for expansion.

"We plan to issue US$90 million in convertible bonds to raise funds for our expansion. The bonds will be listed in Luxembourg in June," company vice-president Chang Shui-wang told Reuters by telephone.
Part of the funds will also be used to pay back bank loans and to purchase raw materials overseas, Chang said.
Other details have yet to be decided, Chang said.
The firm would start its T$4 billion expansion in July, which is expected to be completed by the end of 1999, he said.
The expansion includes a steel pickling line, a cold-rolling mill, a galvanising line and a pre-coating line.
Yieh Phui is a key member of the Yieh Loong steel group, which has two other listed firms -- Yieh Loong and Yieh-Hsing.
